..
While a generally dry period remains through the weekend,
precipitable water remains between 1.75" and 2.25" across all
islands. This moisture is expected to remain along with light and
variable winds, so island effect showers and isolated thunderstorms 
will be possible Sunday and Monday. For Sunday, Guam will have the
highest chance for significant rainfall. Rota may see some lighter
showers. Island-effect showers over Tinian and Saipan will likely 
remain mostly offshore to the west. Weak upper-level support and 
slightly increased shear should allow for some island-effect showers
to produce lightning and last longer than today. By Monday, all 
islands will likely see afternoon showers and isolated 
thunderstorms. For Saipan, these showers will likely build over the 
southwest portion of the island due to a weak northeast wind. By 
Tuesday, westerlies winds ahead of a slowly developing trough may 
prevent further island effect showers, but then bring additional 
monsoon moisture into the region sometime Wednesday. This will bring 
shower coverage back to scattered with isolated thunderstorms 
possible. This trough will be closely monitored for any potential 
impacts to the Marianas late next week. Models currently indicate it 
drifting north of the Marianas with a monsoon tail bringing 
precipitation and breezy conditions to the Marianas.

Marine...
Light and variable winds will prevail through Monday. Seas around
3 feet will remain small through Wednesday before likely starting
to increase as the monsoon flow strengthens and moves into the 
Marianas, causing an increased southwest swell. The risk of rip 
currents is currently low along all reefs of the Marianas and is 
expected to stay that way through at least Tuesday. Only a very small
southwest swell and east-northeast swell remains. There will be a 
moderate risk of lightning Sunday afternoon through Monday, and then 
Wednesday night to the end of the forecast period. 

Eastern Micronesia...
The main forecast challenge was determining rainfall potential, as
the monsoon trough lurks in the area of Guam to Majuro. The best 
moisture pooling is located in a broad swath south of the trough 
axis, as you'd expect. However, surface convergence is modest. Here, 
PWATs (Precipitable Water Values) of 2.5 to 2.8 inches are common. 
Kosrae is currently the only location seeing cellular convection 
based on satellite imagery, with Pohnpei and Majuro seeing convective
debris aloft more than anything. Still, given the PWATs and 
potential outflow boundary interactions the next few days, aided by 
at least prolonged modest convergence, we didn't want to go as low as
isolated shower coverage through Monday. As such, the forecast was 
trended towards that scenario for Pohnpei and Kosrae. 

At Majuro though, scattered shower coverage was maintained 
throughout the forecast period as you're closest to the monsoon 
trough, and this looks to remain the case through the middle of next 
week, probably longer.

As for marine conditions, seas of 3 to 5 feet will prevail through
the forecast period, with mainly light to gentle winds expected.

Western Micronesia...
Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms are expected to persist
at Yap through the weekend as a moist, west to southwest monsoonal 
flow lingers across the area, before it slowly lifts northward over 
the next couple of days. Mostly isolated showers are expected to 
continue at Palau through Saturday night before drier conditions 
settle in this weekend. Unsettled weather remains around Chuuk and 
is expected to fill over the evening and overnight hours. This will 
cause scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms to continue 
through Sunday night. Gentle to moderate west to southwest winds will
continue at all sites for the next couple of days with winds easing 
slightly this weekend for Palau and Yap. Generally benign marine 
conditions are expected to prevail through at least the weekend with 
combined seas of 3 to 5 feet expected at all forecast points. Though,
locally choppy seas will be possible near Yap and Chuuk with heavier
showers and thunderstorms.
